bug_semantics: Apache Neethi policy normalization (Policy.normalize -> AbstractPolicyOperator.normalizeOperator) resolves wsp:PolicyReference children by registry lookup and then recursively normalizes the referenced Policy's components with no cycle set. A WS-Policy graph where Policy A references Policy B and B references A therefore re-enters normalizeOperator on the same policies until StackOverflowError or an unbounded hang. The pre-3.2.2 TYPE_POLICY_REF branch (3.2.1 AbstractPolicyOperator.java:128-148) looks up the URI, wraps the resolved Policy's children in All, and calls normalizeOperator again; PolicyReference.normalize is only an entry point into that same operator path. Attackers supply or register such a circular document and trigger normalize(true), causing DoS (CWE-400). Patched in 3.2.2 by tracking resolving policy ids and throwing RuntimeException on a repeat.
flaw_origin: The recursive PolicyReference expansion was first written on 2007-06-18 in 8baf24289b8a2976f7df94adac1d1470ec80be13 ("Fixed: The proper normalization of the <wsp:PolicyReference> element."). Parent 1dc43243631039e9f67f89ae0500178dd44e6fd1 already looked up TYPE_POLICY_REF but did not recurse; 8baf242 added AbstractPolicyOperator.java:118-120 which copies the resolved Policy's components into All and calls normalizeOperator(all, reg, deep) with no visiting set. 1a8ffd6 (2006-09-18) introduced the lookup-only branch and is not the DoS. Later e174c261 (2011-07-06) only added a Policy parameter and #id fallback on the same recursive call (refactor, not a new mechanism).

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-42403 is a real published Apache CNA record (not withdrawn). The mechanism is unbounded recursion in AbstractPolicyOperator.normalizeOperator when expanding TYPE_POLICY_REF. Policy.normalize(reg, deep) always enters that operator; circular A<->B registry policies, as in the 3.2.2 unit test, overflow the stack. Direct fix 7a38f2be139d70fbf879fbb54eebe1fde633cc32 is the first commit that adds a resolving set; it is in neethi-3.2.2 and not in neethi-3.2.1, matching the advisory boundary. BIC search used -S/-L/blame on the recursive TYPE_POLICY_REF expansion rather than scanning for AI commits. The lookup-only 2006 branch (1a8ffd6) cannot loop. 8baf24289b8a2976f7df94adac1d1470ec80be13 is the smallest first-write of the recursive call; its immediate parent tree lacks those three lines; it is a focused non-merge, non-squash git-svn-era commit. The 2011 signature change is a refactor of the same call. AI judgment is BIC-only: 2007 human Apache author/committer, no commit-object AI marker, therefore NOT_AI.
